Turmeric Market Survey — Ghana R1 — reissued 15 Oct

Frontline workers in Ghana visit turmeric sellers in local markets and complete one short survey for each seller — what kinds of turmeric they sell, the price, how much is in stock, and photographs taken with a yellow MTN scratchcard laid beside the turmeric so that colour and size can be compared fairly across different markets, phones and lighting. The card is the fixed reference that makes photographs from different handsets and different light comparable to each other; without one, a brighter photograph cannot be told from a brighter turmeric. No physical samples are ever collected. Workers observe, photograph with the card in frame, and ask questions. Nothing physical leaves the seller, no laboratory or chemical testing is done, and the programme makes no judgement, score or claim about any seller's product. Archetype: atomic-visit. One short, self-contained survey per seller, with no follow-up and no repeat visit to the same seller. Workers first complete an eight-menu Learn app and must pass a certification quiz at 80% before any survey work is unlocked. A separate unpaid Contact Log records approaches that are not turmeric-seller surveys (a refusal, a closed stall, a seller who does not sell turmeric) so those do not consume a worker's paid survey allocation. A survey is paid when it was started between 07:00 and 19:00 Ghana time, took at least five minutes from opening to sending, recorded consent, and recorded that the seller does sell turmeric. Nothing else affects payment — not photograph quality, not price, not any other survey content. Duplicate-seller review and photograph-quality review are human review activities and never gate or reverse a payment. Round 1 of 2. This round is a review build: the implementing organisation (tekzal) works through the training and survey apps end to end and returns feedback before any wider collection. The deployment round is designed after this round's feedback and runs as a separate engagement.

Turmeric Market Survey (Atomic Visit) — Ghana 2026

Atomic-visit market survey in Ghana. Certified frontline workers visit turmeric sellers in local markets and complete one standardized survey per seller, recording the forms of turmeric on sale, price and availability, packaging and any volunteered origin, alongside reference-calibrated photographs taken with a yellow MTN scratchcard laid flat in frame as a fixed colour and size reference. Location, timestamps and duration attach automatically. The output is a consistent, comparable, geo-tagged picture of turmeric market presence across sellers and markets. The programme addresses the comparability problem, not the chemistry problem: it makes no laboratory determination and no safety or quality claim about any seller's product, and no physical samples are collected. Single-stage, one record per seller, no follow-up visits. Payment is per verified seller survey on automatic criteria — consent given and the seller sells turmeric — within caps of 15 paid surveys per worker per day and 100 per worker in total. Rates are GHS 7 to the worker and GHS 4 to the implementing organisation per verified survey, against a campaign target of 1,000 surveys across up to 10 workers.
